 Tuesday, November 17 Las Vegas, NV 4:30 PM Florida Gators
 vs Notre Dame
 Game Coverage: Watch Listen Live Stats Game Notes Point guard Boogie Fland (0) was a full-go at practice Monday in advance of the Players Era 8 at Las Vegas. Rotation Options Increase For Players Era Gauntlet
 Tuesday, November 17, 2026 | Men's Basketball, Chris Harry
 Share: By: Chris Harry, Senior Writer 
 LAS VEGAS  – Inside two minutes remained in the first half Friday night, with Florida on a run when the Gators threw a 1-2-2 press at Merrimack. Backup forward Domen Petrovic was at the top and Alex Lloyd , in his first career start, was on the second line. 
As the Warriors tried to swing the ball horizontally across the floor, forward Thomas Haugh , playing on the back end, saw the play developing – with Petrovic disrupting the ball-handler – and yelled for his teammate to chase the next pass.
 "Go get it, Lloyd!"  
And get it, he did. Lloyd picked off the play and raced to the rim for a dunk and two of his career-high 11 points that included three 3-pointers. 
"We see Lloyd-o do it at practice all the time, so it wasn't surprising," Haugh said. "For him to do it in a game, though, hopefully the confidence will carry over. We're going to need him, just like we've needed some of those other guys on the bench who have been stepping up."  
 Alex Lloyd answer (4) the call for his first career start last week with 11 points against Merrimack. 
In that aforementioned sequence last week, it was the first time during this young season the combination of Petrovic, Lloyd, Haugh, guard Urban Klavzar and center Rueben Chinyelu were on the floor at the same time. Lloyd was in the game because starting point guard Boogie Fland was held out with a sore shoulder that he rested over the weekend in anticipation of this week's three-day paddle-wheel of power conference opponents that starts Tuesday when the No. 1 Gators (4-0) face unbeaten Notre Dame (4-0) in opening-round play of the Players Era 8 at Michelob ULTRA Arena. 
 [Read senior writer Chris Harry 's "Pregame Stuff" setup here ] 
There could very well will be other first-time rotations unveiled this week, what the tournament's three-games-in-three-days format and potential match-ups against Houston and Kansas – both loaded and considered national-championship caliber – among the scenarios. 
Fland, the speedy playmaker and defensive ball hawk, returned to practice Sunday before the team's charter flew out of Gainesville. He was full-go during Monday's workout at UNLV. 
Coach Todd Golden 's rotation choices increased with Lloyd in the mix, giving the Gators nine players, versus leaning so heavily on Haugh, Chinyelu and forward Alex Condon playing 30-plus minutes like they did in wins over Miami and Florida State.
 (Also worth noting: Sophomore wing CJ Ingram (back) is nearing a return to contact work, but that's a different and later conversation.) 
"It's going to be a great measuring stick for where we are," Golden said of the tournament. "It's a great challenge for us, because we like to play pretty physical, and we play three days in a row. We're going to have to see more bodies. We're going to have to see our bench step up, for sure. We're not going to be able to play guys 36 minutes three days in a row, so it's going to provide an opportunity for others."
Rewind a few weeks to the UF preseason when the Gators played a closed scrimmage against North Florida (win) and exhibition games against Baylor (loss) and Stetson (win). The Florida reserves did not distinguish themselves in any of those outings, especially the latter two outings when they were outscored by the opposing benches a combined 61-7.
But junior guard/forward Isaiah Brown (5.5 points, 2.8 rebounds) and the rookie 6-foot-9 Petrovic (3.3 points, 2.5 rebounds) have since provided some reliable pop through the first four games, alongside Klavzar, the 2026 Southeastern Conference Sixth Man of the Year.  
 Alex Lloyd (left) gets dabbed up by Coach Todd Golden during Monday's practice at UNLV. 
Toss Lloyd into the fray – "There's more trust there now with the coaches," Fland said – and the Gators look a little deeper than they did even a week ago, and maybe added a shooting threat on the perimeter. Lloyd went 3-for-6 from deep against Merrimack.
"He's someone we can look at as a viable option," said UF associate head coach Carlin Hartman , who coaches the reserves during scrimmages. "We traditionally haven't played a lot of guys, but that kind of performance [by Lloyd] is going to give Coach Golden and our staff a little more confidence to put him in there."
OK, so the bench may not be as long as Las Vegas Boulevard, but the four guys most likely to get the call are averaging a combined 24.1 points. Collectively, the Florida bench has a plus-46 floor score through four games and has outscored the opposing bench in each game. 
"We're a lot further along rotation-wise this year than we were last year, and the exhibition season probably helped us with that a little bit, trying some things out," Golden said. "We feel like we pulled the right levers in terms of our rotation going into that first game. We played well against Miami, we played well at Florida State. So going in [to Vegas], we'll be pretty consistent with that. I do think we'll play a deeper bench."
The trip to the desert is UF's second in barely 12 months, but under very different circumstances. 
Florida was reigning national champion and ranked third in the country when in came to Vegas to open the 2025-26 season against 17 th -ranked Arizona about a half-mile away at T-Mobile Arena. Those Gators, like the current version, returned a loaded front court, but Haugh was playing for the first time on the wing and the team was debuting a new backcourt of Fland and Xaivian Lee against a terrific Wildcats squad that eventually reached the Final Four. 
UF didn't guard particularly well that day, fouled and turned the ball over too much, shot poorly from the floor and 3-point line, and eventually lost 93-87. 
This Gators team is far more settled-in than that one. And instead of figuring out how to play with each other, they'll use this trip to the Strip perhaps to roll additional pieces into the fold. 
"We didn't play great, we didn't play bad, and Arizona ended up being really good," Golden said of last year's Vegas excursion. "So, I do believe that we're in a much healthier place going out there this year. I'm not sure how much we'll draw on that experience, but I do think getting away from home a little bit, leaving the state, will be good for us to kind of get into our own team bubble, so to speak, and see what we got."
